raw_response:
I am seventy years old now, and I have never been to school. But I have worked this land since I was a boy, so I know what my body can still handle and what it cannot. I have six mu in total. I used to do the wheat-maize double crop like everyone else, but at my age the June harvest and rush to replant maize is too hard on my back. So I switched to single cropping. 

This year I will plant four mu of summer maize and two mu of spring cotton. The maize gives me grain to eat and to feed my few chickens and pigs, and the cotton brings in cash at the market. I will buy hybrid maize seeds—longping208—from the seed shop in town. For the cotton I will just buy whatever hybrid seed the shop has; I do not read the bags, but the shopkeeper knows me. 

I will rotary till both fields because it is easier than ploughing with an animal. For fertilizer I will spread 150 jin per mu of the compound bag from the cooperative—28-6-6 on the maize and 16-14-18 on the cotton. I will irrigate twice, once when the dry spell hits in July and again in August if the soil looks thirsty. Cotton always has bollworms, so I will spray insecticide many times—about fifteen times through the season—and once with herbicide. The maize only needs one spray for insects and one for weeds. I expect to get around 1,020 jin per mu from the maize and about 520 jin per mu from the cotton. That is enough for me.
